prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: العربية · المنتجات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المنتج" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 97px
  col 2: header "السعر" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 70px
  col 3: header "المخزون" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 445px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r0B: widths [96, 91, 74, 98] · table 360×531px · row heights [36, 176, 60, 199, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [116, 91, 74, 78] · table 360×671px · row heights [36, 269, 60, 246, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1A: widths [71, 91, 74, 123] · table 360×438px · row heights [36, 129, 60, 153, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [71, 76, 74, 138] · table 360×392px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 129, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [71, 93, 74, 121] · table 360×438px · row heights [36, 129, 60, 153, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [82, 91, 74, 112] · table 360×485px · row heights [36, 153, 60, 176, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [71, 68, 74, 146] · table 360×392px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 129, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [71, 91, 74, 123] · table 360×438px · row heights [36, 129, 60, 153, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

That preserves numeric scanning and word integrity while keeping the table at 438px rather than 531–671px. r1B/r2C are publishable compact alternatives, but they wrap ر.س under every price; r2B is a milder tradeoff that improves product wrapping at the cost of a seventh description line.","principles":{"general":["Allocate by content role: short identifiers and numerics get minimum viable widths; the long-text column receives the residual width.","Keep repeated numeric/currency patterns on one line when possible; wrapping them weakens vertical comparison more than a modest height increase.","Judge widths by their line-break consequences, not by equal widths or the shortest table alone.","In RTL tables the visual order reverses, so the long prose column may be the leftmost column rather than the rightmost."],"specific":["At 71px, Arabic product names wrap cleanly without mid-word splits, though 'شاشة 27 بوصة' takes three lines; at about 82px it takes two.","The price column needs 91px to keep '3,200 ر.س' on one line; 76px and 68px wrap the currency onto a second line.","الوصف drives row heights: 123px gives 6 lines, 138px gives 5, 112px gives 7, 98px gives 8, and 78px gives 11.","On the 360px canvas, after 71+91+74px for product, price, and stock, only 123px remains for الوصف."]},"tradeoffs":"One-line prices versus a roughly 46px shorter table; product-name readability versus description width; r2B's extra product width versus its 47px height penalty. The 2px difference between r1A and r2A is below perceptual significance.","uncertain":"Whether wrapping ر.س under each price is acceptable on a phone-sized table; the exact description line-break thresholds between 112px and 138px; and whether r2B's cleaner product wrapping justifies its extra height."}
